name: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
venue: ICLR 2023 (International Conference on Learning Representations 2023; arXiv preprint submitted Oct 2022, v3 camera-ready Mar 2023)
authors_affiliation: Shunyu Yao (work partly done at Google Brain), Jeffrey Zhao, Dian Yu, Nan Du, Izhak Shafran, Karthik Narasimhan, Yuan Cao. Primary affiliations: Department of Computer Science, Princeton University (Yao, Narasimhan) and Google Research / Brain team (Zhao, Yu, Du, Shafran, Cao).
code_url: https://github.com/ysymyth/ReAct (official GPT-3 prompting code for the ICLR 2023 paper)
maintained_repo_url: N/A (single research repo; no continuously-maintained leaderboard. The README points users to LangChain's ReAct agent implementation for broader use)
task_domain: Multi-domain: knowledge-intensive QA (HotpotQA), fact verification (FEVER), embodied/text-based decision making (ALFWorld), and web navigation / online shopping (WebShop). The method is a general reasoning-and-acting prompting paradigm spanning QA, tool-use (Wikipedia API), embodied, and web tasks.
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent, few-shot (in-context) prompting setting with a frozen LLM (primarily PaLM-540B; also GPT-3 text-davinci-002). The agent operates in a closed loop with an external environment: at each step the LLM generates either a free-form reasoning trace (thought) or a task-specific action; actions are executed against an external source (a Wikipedia search API for QA/fact-verification, or the ALFWorld/WebShop environment) which returns an observation appended to the context, and the loop continues until a finish/answer action. Supervision is only 1-6 hand-written ReAct-format exemplars per task (no gradient updates at inference). The paper also reports an optional bootstrapped finetuning setting using 3,000 ReAct trajectories with correct answers to finetune smaller PaLM-8B/62B models.
what_is_retrieved: docs / external knowledge: for QA and fact verification, the agent retrieves short Wikipedia passages (first 5 sentences of an entity page) and lookup hits via a simple Wikipedia web API; the actions also gather environment observations (state descriptions) in ALFWorld and product/page text in WebShop. Few-shot ReAct exemplars (human-written reasoning+action trajectories) are provided in the prompt but are fixed, not retrieved per query.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: retrieval (via the Wikipedia search/lookup API) targets a fixed external knowledge base (Wikipedia) / the external environment state. There is no agent-written, growing episodic memory store that retrieval indexes into; the LLM is frozen and the corpus is static.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Neither a learned top-k ranking nor a completeness objective in the retriever sense. Retrieval is a single deterministic API lookup per action: search[entity] returns the first 5 sentences of the matching page (or top-5 similar entity name suggestions if no exact match), and lookup[string] returns the next sentence containing the string. The 'completeness' of evidence is driven by the LLM's iterative reasoning deciding which entities to search next, not by a ranking objective. The paper explicitly notes this API is deliberately weaker than SOTA lexical/neural retrievers.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not a case-based-reasoning method; no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain case cycle is implemented).
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner. It is positioned as a reasoning-and-acting prompting paradigm.
retrieval_unit: document / snippet: a short Wikipedia passage (first 5 sentences of an entity page) or a single lookup sentence per action; in decision-making tasks the retrieved unit is an environment observation (text state description, product listing/option text). The retrievable in-context exemplars are full human-written ReAct trajectories (thought-action-observation sequences).
index_source: Static external corpus: Wikipedia accessed live through a simple search/lookup web API (no offline-induced or test-time-grown private index). For decision tasks, observations come from the static ALFWorld simulator and the WebShop environment (1.18M real-world products). No growing/learned retrievable store.
index_structure_topology: Flat / API-keyed: the Wikipedia API is keyed by exact entity/page name (search) and by substring match within a page (lookup); it is not a vector index, graph, or hierarchical store built by the authors. WebShop is a website search index (keyword search over product catalog). No custom index topology is constructed.
retriever_type: Off-the-shelf keyword/exact-match API (lexical lookup): the Wikipedia search engine + a Ctrl+F-style substring lookup; for WebShop a built-in keyword product search. There is no dense, learned, or generative retriever trained by the authors; the LLM acts as the policy that issues queries.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf). The retrieval API itself is not trained. The LLM's decision of WHAT to search/look up is shaped only by the few-shot in-context ReAct exemplars (no gradient training of a retriever). In the optional finetuning variant, the whole trajectory generator (including action/query choices) is bootstrap-finetuned on 3,000 self-generated correct trajectories, but this trains the policy LM, not a separate retriever.
query_construction: Thought-conditioned, LLM-generated queries: the model emits a reasoning thought (e.g. 'I need to search x, find y, then find z') and then issues a search[entity] or lookup[string] action whose argument is generated by the LLM. Queries can be reformulated across steps ('maybe I can search/look up x instead'). The query is composed online from the model's evolving reasoning, not from the raw input alone.
query_granularity: Step/state-level: a new query (search or lookup action) can be constructed at each step of the interleaved reasoning-acting loop, conditioned on the current thought and prior observations, rather than once at t=0.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative / agent-initiated: retrieval happens whenever the LLM decides to emit an action (vs. a thought) during the reasoning-acting loop; the model itself chooses when to think and when to act/retrieve. Multiple retrieval steps per task instance (up to a step cap, e.g. 7 steps on HotpotQA, 5 on FEVER).
retrieval_trigger_signal: Agent-initiated request: the LLM-generated decision to output an action (search/lookup) rather than a thought is the trigger. There is no explicit token-confidence, attention-uncertainty, or learned-classifier trigger; the model's prompted policy interleaves thoughts and retrieval actions freely. (At the task level, a heuristic backoff exists: ReACT->CoT-SC switches to internal-knowledge reasoning if no answer is returned within the step budget, and CoT-SC->ReAct switches to acting when CoT-SC majority confidence is below n/2.)
reranking: None. No reranking stage; the Wikipedia API returns a fixed-format result (first 5 sentences, or top-5 similar entity name suggestions) consumed directly as the observation.
retrieved_context_refinement: None / minimal: retrieved Wikipedia text is returned in a truncated form by design (first 5 sentences via search, single next sentence via lookup), which acts as a coarse built-in truncation, but there is no learned distillation, decompose-recompose, distractor filtering, or compression of the retrieved content. The LLM's own reasoning then extracts/interprets the relevant facts in subsequent thoughts.
tool_document_engineering: N/A: the action set (search/lookup/finish) is described directly in the few-shot prompt via exemplar trajectories rather than indexed tool documents; no synthetic-query augmentation, expanded summaries, or instruction-tuned tool embeddings.
index_content_separation: N/A: no separation of a lightweight retrievable index from heavy on-demand content; the Wikipedia API simply returns truncated page text on each call.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A: a single fixed Wikipedia web API (custom search/lookup/finish) and the WebShop/ALFWorld environment interfaces; no live-synchronized tool index, RapidAPI/RESTful catalog, MCP, or function-calling registry, and no CRUD auto-sync.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A: no modeling of inter-tool dependencies; the small fixed action space (search, lookup, finish, or environment-specific actions) has no dependency graph or prerequisite modeling beyond the LLM's reasoning.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation in a closed loop: each retrieved observation (Wikipedia passage, environment state, product text) is appended to the running context, and the LLM reasons over the accumulated thought-action-observation stream to decide the next thought/action and ultimately the final answer. The few-shot ReAct exemplars are used as in-context demonstrations of the reason-act-observe format. Retrieved/observed information directly grounds the model's reasoning and final answer synthesis.
planning_integration: Per-step interleaved retrieve-and-act within a single closed-loop trajectory: reasoning traces induce, track, and update the action plan, handle exceptions, and decide search reformulation, while actions interface with external sources; retrieval/acting and planning are woven together step by step (no separate plan-then-retrieve phase, no tree search/MCTS). Reasoning helps plan acting; acting (retrieval) supplies information that updates the plan.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-tool-call / per-step within a rollout: thoughts (reasoning) and actions (incl. search/lookup tool calls) are interleaved at the step level. For QA the prompt uses 'dense' thoughts (a thought before nearly every action); for decision-making tasks (ALFWorld/WebShop) the prompt uses 'sparse' thoughts (the LM decides when to think vs. act), so reasoning is woven per-action rather than per-token.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (no case adaptation; not a CBR method). The few-shot ReAct exemplars are used as verbatim in-context demonstrations of format/strategy, and the LLM generalizes from them in-context.
retrieved_item_representation: Surface form is raw text: retrieved Wikipedia passages and environment observations are injected as raw text observations interleaved with the model's free-text thoughts and actions. In-context exemplars are raw human-written reason-act-observe trajectories. No distilled strategy, executable program, or latent token representation.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw text evidence/observation (low abstraction): short raw Wikipedia passages / raw environment state descriptions, not distilled strategies or workflows. The in-context exemplars are raw demonstration trajectories.
noise_robustness_mechanism: LLM self-reflection via reasoning, plus a hybrid-backoff strategy: free-form thoughts let the model recognize non-informative searches and reformulate queries; the paper analyzes that non-informative search derails reasoning (23% of error cases). To combat both hallucination (CoT) and unhelpful retrieval (ReAct), the authors propose combining ReAct with CoT-SC (ReAct->CoT-SC and CoT-SC->ReAct) so the model falls back to internal knowledge when retrieval fails and to retrieval when internal-knowledge confidence is low. No retriever-aware training or learned relevance evaluator.
memory_type: none (within a task instance, the running context window acts as transient working memory of the thought-action-observation stream; there is no persistent episodic store, skill library, or graph memory that carries across tasks).
write_back: False: the system does not store new experiences/cases/skills into a persistent retrievable memory at inference. (The optional offline finetuning bootstraps 3,000 self-generated correct trajectories into model weights, but this is offline training, not an inference-time write-back memory.)
online_growth: No: no retrievable store grows during deployment/test-time; the LLM is frozen and the Wikipedia corpus is static. The only growth-like step is offline bootstrapped finetuning on pre-collected trajectories.
write_back_trigger: Never (at inference): no memory write occurs during the reasoning-acting loop. In the optional finetuning pipeline, trajectory collection is on-success-only (only ReAct trajectories that reached correct answers are used to finetune), but this is an offline training-data step, not an online write-back.
failure_experience_usage: Success-only: the optional finetuning uses only trajectories with correct final answers (3,000 correct-answer trajectories); failed/negative trajectories are not stored or retrieved. At inference there is no failure memory; the model can react to a failed/non-informative search only within the current context window via reasoning.
memory_evolution_update: N/A / not applicable (no persistent stored entries to mutate). Within a task, context is append-only (each thought/action/observation is appended), but there is no cross-task memory evolution, dedup, or pruning.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Partially: retrieval is not a fixed similarity top-k. The LLM acts as the policy deciding when and what to retrieve, driven by in-context few-shot prompting (not an RL/value-based learned selection policy). The optional finetuning bootstraps this acting policy into smaller models via supervised imitation on self-generated correct trajectories, but it is not RL or a learned ranking policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No: single-agent, single-model; no memory/experience sharing across multiple agents or frameworks.
benchmarks: HotpotQA (multi-hop QA, 500-question validation subset), FEVER (fact verification), ALFWorld (text-based embodied household game, 134 unseen evaluation games, 6 task types), WebShop (online shopping web navigation, 1.18M products, 12k instructions, 600 test instructions). Base LLMs: PaLM-540B (main) and GPT-3 text-davinci-002 (confirmatory). Finetuning uses PaLM-8B/62B.
benchmark_family: QA / multi-hop (HotpotQA), fact-verification (FEVER), embodied (ALFWorld), web (WebShop). Spans the QA, embodied, and web families.
baselines: Prompting baselines (systematic ablations of ReAct): Standard (no thoughts/actions/observations), CoT (chain-of-thought, reasoning-only), CoT-SC (self-consistency over CoT samples), Act (acting-only, no thoughts), and hybrids ReAct+CoT-SC and CoT-SC+ReAct. Decision-making baselines: BUTLER and BUTLER_R (imitation-learning agents) on ALFWorld; ReAct-IM (Inner Monologue style dense-feedback ablation) on ALFWorld; imitation learning (IL) and imitation+RL (IL+RL) agents, plus expert Human, on WebShop. Reference SOTA fine-tuned methods are cited (e.g. on HotpotQA/FEVER) as context but not directly beaten by the prompting methods.
key_metrics: HotpotQA: exact match (EM). FEVER: accuracy. ALFWorld: task-specific success rate (%). WebShop: average score (% of desired attributes covered) and success rate (% of episodes satisfying all requirements). Also qualitative human-labeled success/failure mode analysis (e.g. hallucination/false-positive rates).
headline_result: On the two interactive decision-making benchmarks, ReAct outperforms imitation and reinforcement learning methods by an absolute success-rate improvement of 34% on ALFWorld and 10% on WebShop, while being prompted with only one or two in-context examples (ICLR camera-ready abstract). Concretely on ALFWorld the best ReAct trial reaches 71% average success vs. best Act 45% and BUTLER 37%; on WebShop ReAct gives an absolute +10% success rate over the previous best. (Note: the arXiv v3 abstract states 34% for ALFWorld; the older PDF body text in one place states 44% — the canonical/camera-ready figure is 34%.)
ablations: Extensive systematic ablations: (1) ReAct vs. Act (removing thoughts) shows reasoning helps acting on all tasks; on ALFWorld ReAct (71% best) >> Act (45% best), with relative gains 33%-90% (avg 62%) across six controlled trials. (2) ReAct vs. CoT on QA/FEVER: ReAct beats CoT on FEVER (60.9 vs 56.3) but slightly trails CoT on HotpotQA (EM 27.4 vs 29.4); human analysis shows CoT hallucinates more (false-positive 14% vs 6%; 56% of CoT failures are hallucination) while ReAct's failures are more from non-informative search (23% of errors). (3) ReAct+CoT-SC / CoT-SC+ReAct hybrids are best overall and reach 21-sample CoT-SC performance with only 3-5 samples. (4) Finetuning ablation: with 3,000 examples, finetuned ReAct is the best format across sizes; finetuned PaLM-8B ReAct beats all PaLM-62B prompting, and finetuned PaLM-62B ReAct beats all 540B prompting methods. (5) ReAct vs. ReAct-IM (Inner-Monologue-style dense external feedback) on ALFWorld: ReAct (71) >> ReAct-IM (53), confirming the value of flexible internal reasoning over reactive feedback.
evaluation_decoupling: No: there are no separate intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG) reported. Evaluation is end-to-end task performance (EM, accuracy, success rate, score); the retrieval quality is examined only qualitatively (e.g. fraction of non-informative searches in error analysis).
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both outcome and process: primary metrics are outcome-based (EM / accuracy / success rate / score), but the paper adds substantial process analysis -- human-labeled success/failure modes on 50 sampled trajectories (hallucination vs reasoning error vs non-informative search) and explicit discussion of interpretability/trustworthiness of the reasoning-acting trajectories.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Few-shot efficiency emphasized: ReAct uses only 1-2 (decision tasks) or 3-6 (QA/FEVER) in-context exemplars yet beats IL/RL baselines trained on 10^3 to 10^9 task instances. Hybrid ReAct+CoT-SC matches 21-sample CoT-SC accuracy using only 3-5 samples (large sampling-cost saving). Step budgets are small (7 steps HotpotQA, 5 steps FEVER; trajectories needing the full budget are <2% of correct cases). No explicit token/API-dollar latency table is reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed small prompt budget: 6 ReAct exemplars for HotpotQA, 3 for FEVER, and 1-2 for the decision-making tasks (ALFWorld uses 2 of 3 annotated trajectories per task type via permutation; WebShop one/two-shot). Retrieval per action returns a capped amount (first 5 sentences for search, one sentence for lookup, top-5 similar entity suggestions on miss). Step caps bound the trajectory length (e.g. 7/5 steps). Selection count is fixed/heuristic, not adaptive or reranked-then-truncated.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (not a benchmark-construction paper; it evaluates on existing benchmarks -- HotpotQA, FEVER, ALFWorld, WebShop).
builds_on: Chain-of-Thought prompting (Wei et al., 2022) and CoT self-consistency (Wang et al., 2022) for the reasoning side; action-generation / LLM-as-policy work such as WebGPT (Nakano et al., 2021), SayCan, and Inner Monologue (Huang et al., 2022) for the acting side; STaR (Zelikman et al., 2022) for the bootstrapped self-generated-trajectory finetuning. Built on frozen PaLM-540B and GPT-3 (text-davinci-002). Evaluation environments build on HotpotQA, FEVER, ALFWorld/ALFRED, and WebShop.
contrasts_with: Reasoning-only methods (CoT, CoT-SC, zero-shot-CoT, Selection-Inference, Faithful Reasoning, Scratchpad) that do not interact with external sources and hallucinate; acting-only / decision-making LLM policies (WebGPT, BlenderBot, Sparrow, SimpleTOD) that do not explicitly model reasoning and rely on expensive human feedback / RL; Inner Monologue (ReAct-IM ablation) whose 'inner monologue' is limited to environment-state observations rather than flexible reasoning; imitation/RL agents (BUTLER, IL, IL+RL) trained on large datasets.
lineage: Foundational paradigm in the B (RAG / agentic task-solving) lineage: ReAct establishes the interleaved reason-act-observe loop that grounds LLM reasoning in external retrieval/tool calls, a precursor to subsequent retrieval-augmented planning, tool-use agents, and reflection/memory methods (e.g. Reflexion, Toolformer-style tool agents, and agent frameworks like LangChain's ReAct agent).
